nodes.title: This is NOT the target framerate

widgets_values: Skip frames is a list of frames that won't be interpolated. Use the ADJUSTED VIDEO PREVIEW frame count to check the frame numbers

nodes.title: INSTRUCTIONS
widgets_values:
### Video settings

- **Custom framerate:** Sets the base frame rate of the source video. **THIS IS NOT YOUR TARGET FRAMERATE.** It defines the frame rate you want to force on the source video. Set this value to `0` to use the original frame rate.
- **Max duration:** Sets a length limit (in seconds) for the final video *(requires a custom framerate value)*. Set this value to `0` to process the entire video.
- **Skip first n seconds:** Skips a portion of the source video from the start *(requires a custom framerate value)*.
- **FPS multiplier:** Not necessary unless interpolation is enabled. This multiplies the base framerate during interpolation.  
  **Example:** If your base framerate is 15 FPS:  
  - Multiplier `2` → 30 FPS video result  
  - Multiplier `4` → 60 FPS video result
- **Aspect ratio crop:** Adjusts the source video to a standard aspect ratio. Select the ratio closest to the source video. If the source is not in a standard aspect ratio, it will be cropped—choose the crop method (top-center, bottom-center, center, etc.). A preview is shown in the **"ADJUSTED VIDEO PREVIEW"**.
- **Target resolution:** Not necessary unless upscaling is enabled. Defines the output resolution for the upscaling process. An RTX 4090 can handle 1440p-60 fps interpolation for 1 minute long videos.

### Main groups

- Enable the **Upscaling** group to upscale the source video.
- Enable the **Interpolation** group to interpolate the source video.

### Optional groups

- **Custom audio:** Allows you to inject custom audio into the final video. This is useful if the original audio degrades after multiple processing passes. The source can be either an audio file or a video.
- **Skip frames in interpolation:** A list of frames to exclude from interpolation.  
  **Example use case:** Videos with scene cuts. Interpolating across cuts can cause a "morphing" effect instead of a clean transition.  
  You can find frame numbers in the **"ADJUSTED VIDEO PREVIEW"**, but note:  
  - The preview starts at frame `1`  
  - The interpolation node starts at frame `0`  
  - Example: To skip frame `100` in the preview, enter `99`
- **Color correction:** Adjusts brightness, contrast, and saturation of the final video.
- **Noise:** AI-generated videos can look overly sharp or "too perfect." This adds subtle noise to make the result look more natural.
- **Trim:** A fallback tool to adjust the final video length. Useful if you forgot to properly set the duration earlier and don’t want to reprocess everything.

### Tips

- Both the **Upscaling** and **Interpolation** groups save their output videos. If ComfyUI crashes, you can reuse the saved video as a new source and continue processing, disabling any steps you’ve already completed.

You can delete this SystemNotification node, it is not relevant at all. It sends a system notification via your browser when the workflow finish execution; it requires an SSL connection for non localhost setups.
